o.text: Ultimately borrowed from Russian па́мперс (pámpers), from the genericized trademark Pampers, from English pamper.
From Proto-Turkic *tȫg- (“to pound”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (tög-, “to pound, crush”), Turkish dövmek.

Most likely reborrowed from Persian تپانچه (tapânča), from Ottoman Turkish طبانجه (tabanca, “palm of the hand; slap; trigger of a gun; handgun”), derived from طبان (taban, “sole”), corresponding to Azerbaijani daban (“heel”).
Borrowed from Russian костю́м (kostjúm), from French costume.

PIE word
 *kʷetwóres
Borrowed from Classical Persian چَارْطَاق (čārtāq, literally “four arches”).
